connections.source_concept: Muon orthogonalised momentum for matrix-shaped parameters
connections.target_problem: Epochs to target for conv filters on CIFAR-100
connections.shared_structure: Matrix-shaped weights whose raw momentum updates are dominated by a few directions
connections.proposed_mechanism: Equalised update spectra make each step more useful early in training
connections.testable_prediction: At the selected base, Muon reaches the matched accuracy in at least 10% fewer epochs than SGD with lookahead
connections.failure_condition: No time gain beyond seed noise at matched accuracy

connections.source_domain: ImageNet speedruns (FFCV, fast.ai DAWNBench) and the Fulcrum CIFAR-10 record
connections.source_concept: Progressive resizing with low resolution early
connections.target_problem: Per-epoch cost early in CIFAR-100 training
connections.shared_structure: Early epochs learn coarse features that survive downsampling
important_differences: 32 px images leave little resolution headroom
100 fine-grained classes may need detail earlier
connections.proposed_mechanism: Bilinear-downsampled 24-28 px epochs cost about 44-23% fewer FLOPs
connections.testable_prediction: A 24 to 28 to 32 px schedule lowers time at matched accuracy by at least 5%
connections.failure_condition: Matched accuracy needs more extra epochs than the resizing saves

design_space.current_assumption: airbench94 widths (64/256/256) with two convs per block suffice for CIFAR-100 at 75%.
alternatives: airbench96 shape (128/384/512, three convs per block with a residual)
design_space.why_material: With 100 classes and no TTA, 75% may be width-limited, which moves the minimum-time point to wider nets.

design_space.current_assumption: airbench tricks (whitening, dirac init, BN-bias lr x64, lookahead, alternating flip, label smoothing 0.2) cut epochs on CIFAR-100 as on CIFAR-10.
design_space.why_material: Epochs to target multiply directly into time.

design_space.current_assumption: Per-epoch time scales with FLOPs at the candidate widths.
alternatives: Small nets launch-bound, so narrower nets save less time than FLOPs suggest
Compile or CUDA graphs change the ranking
design_space.why_material: The airbench paper reports that cutting FLOPs did not cut A100 wall time, so the frontier must be converted with measured A100 times.

design_space.current_assumption: Full 32 px images and all 50,000 examples every epoch.
alternatives: In-run proxy-loss selection of the hardest half of each batch
design_space.why_material: Cheaper epochs can cut time at matched accuracy, but CIFAR-100 tolerates data removal worse than CIFAR-10.

design_space.current_assumption: Per-trial sd near 75% is at most 0.30 pp, so a 75.2% development mean suffices.
alternatives: sd 0.35 to 0.45 pp requiring 75.3% or higher
design_space.why_material: The margin sets the epoch count at the threshold.

hypotheses.proposition: The baseline is overhead-dominated, so ResNet-9 with GPU-resident data, fp16 channels_last and compilation becomes competitive.
hypotheses.mechanism: Removing data-loader, precision and launch overheads cuts per-epoch time without changing epochs to target.
hypotheses.prediction: ResNet-9 per-epoch A100 time falls from 1.48 s to at most 0.7 s at unchanged accuracy.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Per-epoch time stays at or above 1.1 s, consistent with roughly 114 TFLOP per epoch.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Whether ResNet-9 remains a candidate base or only a calibration reference.
evidence_needed: ResNet-9 reference arm accuracy at 40 epochs (P1)

hypotheses.proposition: airbench sample-efficiency tricks transfer to single-view CIFAR-100 and reach 75.3% in at most 20 epochs at some width.
hypotheses.mechanism: Whitening, identity init, BN-bias scaling, lookahead and alternating flip accelerate early optimisation independently of the label space.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one airbench-lineage width reaches a 5-seed mean of 75.3% at 20 epochs or fewer.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: No width reaches 75.3% below about 30 epochs.

hypotheses.proposition: Single-view 75% on CIFAR-100 is capacity-bound, so the minimum-time point sits at airbench95-96 width rather than airbench94 width.
hypotheses.mechanism: Fine-grained 100-way discrimination needs more channels in the late stages than 10-way CIFAR-10.
hypotheses.prediction: The minimum interpolated time at 75.3% occurs at a width multiplier of at least 1.5 or the airbench96 shape.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: The 1x airbench94 width reaches 75.3% at lower interpolated time than every wider arm.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Width and depth of the base regime.

hypotheses.proposition: Muon on conv filters reduces epochs at matched single-view accuracy on CIFAR-100, as it did on CIFAR-10.
hypotheses.mechanism: Orthogonalised momentum updates equalise progress across filter directions, so fewer steps are needed.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% fewer epochs at matched accuracy, with Newton-Schulz overhead under 5% of step time.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: The time gain at matched accuracy lies within seed noise.
evidence_needed: P2 matched-accuracy comparison at the selected base (T-007)

hypotheses.proposition: Cheaper early epochs (progressive resizing or proxy-loss selection) cut time at matched accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Early training extracts coarse features that low resolution or easy-example skipping preserves at lower FLOPs.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 5% lower time at matched accuracy.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: The accuracy loss on CIFAR-100 costs more epochs than the cheaper epochs save.
evidence_needed: P2 matched-accuracy comparison at the selected base (T-007)

hypotheses.proposition: Per-trial sd of single-view accuracy near 75% is at most 0.30 pp for short-budget runs.
hypotheses.mechanism: Short airbench-style runs have test-set sd near the binomial floor reduced by averaging (airbench94: 0.157 pp on CIFAR-10).
hypotheses.prediction: Pooled within-cell sd from P1 cells near 75% is at most 0.30 pp.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Development accuracy target (75.2% versus 75.3% or higher).

observations.statement: The organisers' ResNet-9 baseline (40 epochs, width 64) reached 75.36% mean in 59.30 s on the A100 80GB PCIe over 2 trials; 50 L40 trials gave sd 0.2516 pp.
Untuned airbench96 (40 epochs) reaches 79.27% (flip) and 79.76% (flip+Cutout) on CIFAR-100, both scored with 6-view TTA; single-view CIFAR-100 accuracy is unpublished.
On CIFAR-10 without TTA, Cutout costs 1.14 pp at 10 epochs and 0.38 pp at 20, helps only from about 40 epochs; TTA is worth 0.70-0.79 pp at 10-80 epochs.
A plain ResNet (64/128/256) trained with Muon reaches 70.6% single-view at 16 epochs (one seed, about 26 s on an A100-SXM-64GB).
The substrate's airbench94-equivalent default reaches 69.4-69.7% single-view at 10 epochs on the dev stack (finding F-001), about 5.5 pp short of the target.

omitted_dimensions.rationale: Fixed by RULES.md: single-view, batch 1024, untimed; TTA is banned, so no alternative exists.
Fixed by RULES.md: CIFAR-100 training split only; no external data or pretrained weights.
Fixed by RULES.md: one A100 80GB PCIe; multi-GPU training is out of scope.

probes.method: Run the airbench-lineage substrate through the official harness on the dev stack at width multipliers 1, 1.5 and 2 of 64/256/256 plus the airbench96 shape, at 10, 14, 18 and 24 epochs, five seeds per cell, no Cutout; add a ResNet-9 reference arm at 40 epochs. Collate mean, sd and n per cell and interpolate E*(w) at 75.3%.
probes.decision_rule: Select the width minimising E*(w) times A100 per-epoch time from T-004; if no width reaches 75.3% below 30 epochs, H3 dominates and the next probe moves to wider residual nets with Cutout; if the 1x width wins, shift effort to throughput levers.
probes.information_gain: Separates capacity-bound from throughput-bound accounts and supplies the sd estimate for the margin, in one bounded grid.
probes.resource_bound: About 85 runs of 10-60 s each on two local GPUs, roughly one to two GPU-hours.

probes.method: At the base selected after P1, compare Muon versus SGD with lookahead, progressive resizing and proxy-loss selection at matched accuracy with at least 10 seeds per arm.
probes.decision_rule: Adopt a lever only if its time at matched accuracy is lower with a 95% interval excluding zero.
probes.information_gain: Decides each add-on lever at the regime that will be submitted.
probes.resource_bound: About 60-120 runs on two local GPUs plus A100 timing of adopted levers.

question: Where does the single-view width by epochs frontier cross 75% on CIFAR-100, and is the minimum-time regime capacity-bound or throughput-bound?
synthesis: P1 is the smallest probe that separates the capacity-bound (H3) and throughput-bound (H1, narrow-width H2) accounts and yields the sd estimate for H6; optimiser and data-volume levers (H4, H5) stay dormant until a base is selected.
